The ceiling is also locally verifiable without search:

At Δ=1, renewing before tick 7 increases the charge rate without gaining service; renewing after tick 7 adds only unserved time.

Random mixtures of renewal ages cannot exceed the best deterministic cycle ratio because their long-run ratio is a physical-time-weighted combination of the component ratios.

7. Boundary phase and implementation audit

The frozen phase convention gives the following decisive witnesses:

Δ=1,K=7: cycle length 7, service 7, one charge.

Δ=4,K=1: cycle length 4, service 4, and three residual service ticks are discarded.

Δ=4,K=2: cycle length 8, service 7, one charge.

In each case, service for the ending interval is credited before the renewal action at its ending boundary. The action changes only the following interval.

The permitted B2 host processes its action/renewal logic before computing same-step resource activity and service. It may be a valid definition of the older B2 object, but it cannot be used unmodified as an executable oracle for this cell’s expressly different service-before-boundary-action convention.

That is the most important implementation risk here. An executable result obtained by directly reusing that step ordering could disagree with the exact cell while saying nothing against the mathematics.

8. Counterparameterizations and ambiguities

No admissible interpretation inside the frozen object reverses the branch.

The potentially branch-changing alternatives all modify the scientific object:

Cycle-average error: averaging (service−2)/(ΔK) over cycles instead of taking the regenerative ratio of expectations gives a different estimand.

Opportunity weighting: giving the two strata equal numbers of opportunities or cycles instead of equal physical-time weight changes the aggregate.

Boundary reversal: allowing renewal to affect the interval ending at the same boundary changes min(ΔK,7).

Immediate renewal: permitting K=0 contradicts starting just after renewal and acting only at interval-ending boundaries.

Transform projection: rounding 175/256 back to Q changes the exponential family.

Missing common-rate cap: omitting min(1,Δh) changes the high-h candidates, although it does not affect the actual h=3/16 optimum.

KEEP transient: counting the initial seven serviced ticks as a persistent KEEP rate confuses a finite initial transient with a long-run average.

No. Exact reasoning is sufficient to settle the frozen answer.

An executable enumeration can detect:

incorrect physical-time weighting,

accidental probability projection,

a wrong shell,

or an incorrect tie implementation.

It cannot provide a new scientific observation under the fixed mathematical object. If an implementation returns another branch, the correct conclusion is that it implemented another object or rule until the discrepancy is resolved.

10. Narrowest admissible claim

On this exact seven-tick, cost-two, spacing-{1,4}, equal-physical-time, Q-grid, state-blind memoryless renewal host:

The optimized common executed-rate family has higher direct return than the optimized exponential-survival-link family, but their gap is only approximately 0.01817, below the registered 1/32 margin. The common-rate family is approximately 0.00244 below the unrestricted memoryless grid ceiling and exceeds the optimized shared raw-probability family by approximately 0.13736, more than 1/32. The registered result therefore supports only a local generic physical-rate explanation, not distinct exponential-link value.

Strongest supporting facts

The common-rate optimizer wins the registered direct-return endpoint; it nearly reaches the unrestricted memoryless ceiling; it beats shared raw by far more than the margin; and all KEEP and shell competence controls pass.

Strongest facts against overinterpretation

Exponential and common-rate policies are behaviorally different. Exponential delivers about 0.02773 more service but spends about 0.04590 more in renewal charges. Moreover, the age-conditioned ceiling is about 0.21377 above the unrestricted memoryless ceiling. The cell therefore does not establish behavioral equivalence, global optimality of a common rate, or irrelevance of renewal age.

Surviving local alternatives

The common-rate result can be explained by local physical-time normalization under this cost and objective. Exponential linking can still have service value that is not worth its additional charge. Most importantly, the large age-conditioned gap leaves state-blind memorylessness—not link expressibility—as the principal unresolved restriction.

Smallest genuinely new discriminator

The smallest new policy-information change is a single expiry bit indicating whether the current seven-tick service block has been exhausted. A policy that observes only this bit and renews at the first legal expired boundary attains the exact 75/112 ceiling above. That comparator changes neither task content, learning, grid, cost, lifetime, spacing, nor population; it isolates age information from state-blind link shape. Its value is already analytically determined, so an execution would again be an implementation check rather than new evidence.
